newsitem.title: UK: Dlr steady in Europe, awaits German govt comments.
newsitem.headline: Dlr steady in Europe, awaits German govt comments.

text.p: The dollar held firm above 1.79 marks at the European midsession with trade cautious ahead of expected comments on forex developments at a German cabinet news conference today.
German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said late Tuesday the government would make a statement today calling for a strong mark and strong euro. Waigel is not expected to attend the news conference.
The dollar was knocked lower against the mark in overnight trade on Waigel's comments but recovered back above 1.79 marks in the European session.
Although trade was nervous ahead of today's regular news conference, due at 1230 GMT, analysts expected any currency impact to be limited.

"Waigel has already said the government wants a strong mark and they support a stronger currency," said Adrian Schmidt, economist at Chase Investment Bank in London. "And it has been echoed by the Bundesbank so there is not much to gain by repeating it."
By 1050 GMT, the dollar was trading at 1.7928/38 marks, up from an overnight low of 1.7845 but still short of late Tuesday's fresh 71-month peak of 1.8040 marks.

Dealers said the market was still wary of possible intervention to stem dollar gains too far above the 1.80 dollar/mark level, but scepticism was growing the Bundesbank would resort to such action any time soon.

"Intervention is looking more unlikely and the statements out of Germany are sounding increasingly hollow," said a U.S. bank dealer. "A switch to a variable repo would probably send a much stronger signal to the market and achieve more than intervention could."
Short-term German interest rate futures slumped this week amid expectations of tighter German rates.
Market focus this afternoon is on U.S. June consumer price data, due at 1230 GMT, which is expected to reinforce the subdued inflation outlook in the U.S.

"The market has already factored in a 0.2 rise in headline and core and I can't see it coming in more than that, if anything it will be lower than the market expects," said Gerard Lyons, chief economist at DKB International.

Subdued U.S. data today may cool dollar bulls slightly, but U.S. interest rate rise expectations are already low and analysts were mindful that the recent dollar gains have been on the back of weakness elsewhere.
Dollar/yen was firm in Europe just below 116 yen, extending its gains from Tuesday's clearance of key resistance at 114.50.

Dollar/yen option risk reversals, an indicator of market directional bias, snapped closer to par after their long-standing extreme bias for yen calls as spot's jump allayed nagging concerns of further dollar/yen weakness.
Against the yen, the dollar stood at 115.71/76, down from an intraday peak of 115.93 and just off late Tuesday's European level of 115.88/98.
